steps.description: Registered session 1 (claude / claude-opus-5, high).

Replaced the binary disposition.uat (status walked|waived) with a per-component accounting: attestation + components[], each record carrying component, method (6-value vocabulary), reviewers ({type,count}, distinct humans), evidence, findings and a per-component attestation. Reviewer types and component keys are CLOSED vocabularies - the first makes 'an AI reviewed it' unrecordable (spec decision 9), the second makes a self-assessed confidence score or debt ledger unrecordable. Landed in disposition.py (constants + _validate_uat_block) and mirrored in disposition.schema.json ($defs UatComponentRecord / UatReviewer), which an existing parity test caught me not having done.

New spec key uatComponents parsed by spec_config (omitted vs explicitly-empty kept distinct, and the block-list scan cannot swallow the neighbouring prerequisites: list). check_uat_walk_recorded now reads it: an armed set with no inventory is REFUSED rather than defaulted inert, a declared component with no record is refused and named, an unmatched record is refused as a likely typo, and method 'none'/'not-applicable' with an attestation PASSES. Path-shaped evidence is checked for existence; URLs and free-text (SharePoint/Teams) are not. 61 new tests in test_set113_uat_accounting.py plus falsifiers in the schema parity suite; 280 targeted tests green.

Journaled under OPERATOR authority with the operator's own words from operator-notes.md 2026-08-10 as the attestation. First attempted the same record under authority='ai', which decision_journal refused (exit 5, verification-reduction carve-out) - the refusal the spec calls correct, exercised rather than assumed. A second decision journals the mid-set addition of uatComponents to this set's own spec.
**Cross-provider verification.**
**Required portion of the full test suite.**
**Close-out.**
Registered session 2 (claude / claude-opus-5, high).

Defined the portable scenario model in ai_router/scenario.py: stable kebab-case scenario and step ids, prerequisites, baseline (description/setup/observable), reset, recovery, named checkpoints, and per step an action plus an expected observable result. Closed vocabularies at both levels -- an unknown key is refused, not ignored.

Quarantined driver detail structurally: drivers: is opaque to the model, no renderer receives it, and portable_digest() is taken over the portable half only, so a selector change leaves all four renderings byte-identical. ai_router/scenario_lint.py is the advisory second line for selector-shaped text that leaks into portable prose; five rules, each with a planted violation and a legitimate look-alike.

Rendered four documents from the one source (walkthrough.md, training.md, captions.vtt, chapters.json) via ai_router/scenario_render.py, with --check as the divergence gate over the committed tree. Both prose documents state verbatim that no video is needed and carry the replay rule: reaching any step means replaying a prefix from the baseline or the nearest named checkpoint, never random access. One exemplar authored: docs/walkthroughs/work-explorer-first-look.

Four rounds, all routed to gpt-5-6-sol with anthropic excluded. Discovery fan-out (2 lenses) + supplementary found 3 Majors and 8 nits; remediation-review cycle 1 REJECTED one fix (the CSS-id rule missed button#save) and cycle 2 returned VERIFIED with 3 fix verdicts accepted. One nit disputed with deterministic evidence: byte comparison would fail --check on every Windows clone. $1.90.

All three declared suites run after the last code-changing stage: pytest 4893 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed (228s, run at -n 8 per the operator parallelism cap rather than the declared -n auto, recorded in the run's detail field); mocha 1468 passing (23s); playwright 32 passed (180s) on an idle machine. All three recorded via run_of_record.
**Close-out.**
Registered session 3 (claude / claude-opus-5).

Built the fixture web app (src/test/fixtures/task-board: vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, served over HTTP on an ephemeral port by scripts/web-fixture-server.js) as the stand-in for the .NET/Java/vanilla-JS/Python web targets, which are one platform, not four. Reproduced browser recordVideo WITH A CONTROL by the same method Set 111 S4 used to measure the workbench failure: the same fixed probe run twice, differing only in whether recordVideo was passed. Arm A (passed) drove the UI and wrote a 30374-byte video; arm B (omitted) drove the UI and wrote nothing - the exact inversion of the workbench table. Recorded raw in s3-browser-record-measurement.json and reproducible via scripts/measure-browser-record.js, which exits non-zero if the premise ever stops holding. The video is .webm, not MP4, which is the first evidence for the manifest requirement in step 3.

Shipped ai_router/walkthrough_run.py: a JSONL step-event stream (run-started / started / completed / failed / run-finished) keyed by S2's stable step ids, and an artifact-agnostic run manifest. The parser is lenient about truncation (a killed driver's half-written last line is dropped with a note) and strict about contradiction (unknown kind, out-of-order timestamp, terminal event for a step that never started, a stepId the scenario does not declare). Artifact kinds are a closed vocabulary that names terminal-cast and transcript alongside video, every artifact carries an explicit mediaType, an EMPTY artifact list is valid, and a listed-but-missing file is refused. Timing is anchored honestly: the driver brackets newContext() and reports the width of the bracket as anchor.uncertaintyMillis (6-7ms measured) rather than implying frame accuracy. Caption retiming reuses the existing VTT writer via a windows_ms parameter instead of a second copy - measured drift on the real run was ~0.6s cumulative against the authored estimates. Chapter mapping is the manifest's per-step startMillis/endMillis, so there is no second chapters schema to drift. Per the operator's 2026-08-15 tier-2 hedge, each step's target bounding box is recorded and read by nothing.

One command (npm run walkthrough:web -> scripts/record-web-walkthrough.js) drives the fixture, records it, and produces a watchable captioned result in gitignored .walkthrough-runs/. The driver does NOT parse scenario.yaml - walkthrough_run plan hands it the portable steps plus its own quarantined block as JSON, so the repo keeps one scenario parser. Real run: 5/5 steps, 44.1s, 944KB webm, retimed captions, self-contained index.html. Both degraded paths proven, not asserted: --no-video produces a manifest with no video, an index that says so where the player would be, and no captions sidecar; a planted failing expectation in step 3 yields outcome=failed with steps 4-5 recorded as not-reached rather than absent. Cleanup is deterministic and ordered (events stream, context, browser, server, scratch video dir, each guarded); the output dir is emptied per run but REFUSES a non-empty --out that is not a prior run. Tier-1 emphasis outlines the target and dims the rest, injected by the driver so it works against an app that cannot be edited - and it is released after the action, which a first recording proved necessary: the fixture re-renders its list, destroying the emphasised node and leaving the page grey for the rest of the step.

Four rounds, all routed to gpt-5-6-sol with anthropic excluded. ROUND 1 VERIFIED NOTHING: the work had been committed first and verify_session diffs the working tree against HEAD, so the bundle was empty; both findings correctly said so, but with only spec.md to cite the doc-only cap recorded them at Minor and the round printed 'MINOR-ONLY ... effectively VERIFIED' with instructions to close. Round 2 (--diff-base at the pre-session ref) reviewed the real 4681-line delta and found 1 Critical + 4 Majors = 3 distinct defects, all accepted, none disputed, all sharing one shape: each worked on the bundled fixture and failed on a real consumer app. Round 3 (remediation-review) returned VERIFIED, 3 fix verdicts accepted / 0 rejected, and explicitly resolved the round-1 findings. Round 4 is the A4 delta-scoped review owed because docs/walkthroughs/README.md - classified as shipped, correctly - changed after round 3; also VERIFIED, 0 findings. The round-1 hole was fixed at source rather than by weakening the operator-attested severity cap. $2.2754 across 8 routed calls, stated without netting out the $0.44 that bought no verification.

All three declared suites run to completion after the last code-changing edit and recorded via run_of_record: pytest 4978 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed (235s, at -n 8 per the operator parallelism cap rather than the declared -n auto); mocha 1492 passing (17s, +24 for the new webWalkthroughRecorder suite); playwright 37 passed (180s, +5 for expectation-wait.spec.ts). Layer 3 is owed by this session's own spec step 6 and by L-064-12, since package.json counts as product. The FIRST full pytest run found 5 failures - every one a fixture artifact of the new empty-evidence guard, in files not previously run - so they were fixed and the WHOLE suite re-run rather than re-running the five, which is the point of the policy.
**Close-out.**
Registered session 4 (claude / claude-opus-5, high).

Pass criteria fixed BEFORE the first capture: s4-pilot-criteria.json (machine-readable, read by the harness, digest recorded in every measurement) plus s4-pilot-criteria.md. Seven criteria C1-C7 each with an instrument and, where the claim is unfalsifiable without one, a control. Hardened pre-capture against the two false-pass modes the Step 3.5 routed analysis named: title ambiguity (refuse on multiple matches) and scaling myopia (window-resize variant, and the 100%-scaling limitation recorded rather than papered over). Committed before any capture ran.

Pilot run, twice. Round 1: 10 captures + a supplementary clean run, which found C4 failing -- the last caption cue ended 32-83ms after the recording did, on all eleven. Fixed by holding the recording 750ms past the last step, then the WHOLE pilot was re-run against the fixed recorder rather than patching a number. Round 2: 10/10 clean captures, correlation 0.9996 every time against a decoy at 0.2987, zero occluder pixels with an occluder covering 80.8 percent of the target and holding focus, 0px dimension delta including across a deliberate resize, anchor uncertainty 106-110ms, all three dependency-absent variants named and degrading correctly, 14 cleanup attempts with zero leftovers. OBS confirmed left as found by an independent check, not just by the harness reporting on itself.

Outcome recorded either way, as the spec requires. Machine verdict FAIL on C2 and C7; the spec own bar -- ten consecutive clean captures, no wrong-window capture, no privacy leakage -- was met. C2 leakage measured exactly zero while its detector CONTROL came in at 0.441 against a 0.50 bar, because the occluder doubles as C1 structured decoy and includes browser chrome; deliberately NOT retuned, since adjusting the instrument to pass is the same sin as moving the threshold. C7 cannot be satisfied through OBS at all: four configurations tried, a silent audio track is always muxed. Recorder ships PROVISIONALLY -- waiving a criterion reduces verification, which is inside the hard carve-out, so it goes to the operator as guided-look item A. Six residuals recorded; four follow-on sets reserved with triggers, one of which is satisfied today.

Five verification rounds. Round 1 two-lens discovery (8 blocking), round 2 supplementary (1), rounds 3-4 remediation review, round 5 an OPERATOR-AUTHORIZED round that returned VERIFIED with 0 findings and 0 fix verdicts rejected. Seven distinct defects found and fixed, none disputed -- including two in the instruments built to prevent false positives, and a recorder gate that took three attempts because the first two were prose and a warning rather than a gate. The ADVISORY path-aware critique produced no artifact: google succeeded three times, openai failed three times (once on the servant-integrity guard, twice HTTP 400 from the Responses API while the same models answered five verification calls fine). Recorded as S4-R9 and promoted to Session 6 rather than worked around with a same-provider second critic.

All three expensive suites run after the last code change and recorded: pytest 4986 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed (at the operator 8-worker cap, route journaled per G-004), mocha 1548 passed, Layer 3 playwright 37 passed. Extending the uatComponents inventory broke Set 113 S1 own test, which pinned this spec at four components -- fixed by asserting the exact NAMES instead of a count, which catches strictly more (a dropped entry, a reordered one, and the trailing-comment strip the test was written for) and removes the drift surface.
**Close-out**, including this set's own dogfood UAT — its scenario document plus, if the pilot passed, its own narrated recording — `change-log.md`, and the Step 9 review.
Registered session 5 (claude / claude-opus-5, high) with --total-sessions 8, which is what put the two new tutorial sessions into session-state.json.

Criteria fixed BEFORE the first container run, machine-readable in s5-isolation-criteria.json with prose in s5-isolation-criteria.md. Seven criteria: I1 host-is-invisible (the whole point - a magenta marker held FOREGROUND ON THE HOST must contribute <=0.0005 of any frame, with a positive control >=0.50, plus structural assertions on the run command itself: no --privileged, no host net/ipc/pid/userns, no X11 socket or /dev/dri|snd|video mount), I2 target-is-actually-visible with a BLACK-FRAME GUARD (stddev >= 8.0) because two black images correlate perfectly and headless software rendering is the one place a container fails harder than the host, I3 usable resolution, I4 no camera/audio/host display measured as absent DEVICE NODES rather than as forbidden OBS input kinds, I5 dependency-absent (three induced variants), I6 deterministic cleanup incl. leaving the operator podman machine in its ENTRY state rather than stopping something we do not own, I7 cost recorded with NO threshold on purpose. Reuse from S4 is exact where the claim is unchanged - I1 takes C2 instrument and threshold, I2 takes C1 correlation and decoy, I3 takes C3 tolerance - so a change in result cannot be a change in yardstick. Bar is THREE consecutive clean runs, not S4 ten, and the reduction is argued in writing rather than assumed: ten bought down an intermittent window-selection fault among eleven host windows, which is absent by construction on a one-application display; what is being established here is a PROPERTY, established by the control. Four things a container cannot be asked to meet are named so their absence is a documented decision, not a gap: Windows fidelity, display scaling, window disambiguation, and caption alignment (inherited from C4, not re-measured).

Read before ordering the work, and it changed the order. The operator note reframes the risk as CAPABILITY (a recorder is a facility for an AI-driven process to read the operator display) rather than supply chain, so the plugin measurement runs first because the spec says so and because it may dominate on the supply-chain axis, while knowing it does NOTHING for the capability risk. The Linux fidelity cost is accepted by operator ruling; this session states it in the outcome rather than solving it.

MEASURED, and the cheap mitigation does NOT dominate. OBS --only-bundled-plugins removes exactly ONE module of 25 (obs-backgroundremoval.dll, 4 percent by module count) and OBS logs "Third-party plugins disabled." to confirm the flag took effect. What SURVIVES the flag is the point: 24 bundled modules totalling 317 MB, including obs-browser.dll (a full embedded Chromium/CEF), win-dshow.dll (the DirectShow camera path), the DeckLink SDK, NVIDIA video-effects filters, a VST plugin host, VLC integration and obs-websocket (a scriptable remote-control server). By bytes the removal is larger than by count - the machine-wide plugin dir is 101 MB, mostly one ONNX background-removal model - and both denominators are reported rather than the flattering one. Measured two ways that could have disagreed: static enumeration of all three Windows plugin locations, and OBS launched twice with its own log read back. Harness: scripts/measure-obs-plugin-surface.js, refuses to run without the criteria file and stamps its SHA-256. A parser defect was found and fixed mid-measurement - the first cut matched raw indentation and reported 0 modules for two launches that had plainly loaded 25, because every OBS log line carries a timestamp prefix; that is a defect which reads exactly like a finding, and it is documented in the function it broke.

BUILT AND MEASURED. VS Code on Xvfb inside Podman, captured by ffmpeg x11grab, with ZERO bind mounts - artifacts come out via podman cp afterwards, because a bind mount is a hole in the boundary being measured. Machine verdict PASS: six of six scored criteria, three of three clean runs, scored by a SEPARATE script (container-isolation-verdict.js) that reads the criteria and cannot produce measurements, and refuses to score if the stamped criteria digest no longer matches the file. I1 host-pixel fraction 0.000000 with the detector control at 0.999746; I2 correlation 0.9995, decoy 0.3446, frame stddev 13.61; I3 zero pixel delta; I4 no /dev/video, no /dev/snd, no host X11 socket, video track only; I5 3/3 induced variants failed with named messages; I6 zero containers left, zero volumes, machine in entry state. Image 1722 MB, warm build 46.5s, ~40s per run. TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN INSTRUMENTS were found and are recorded because each produced a clean-looking result worth nothing: the positive control FAILED OPEN (xsetroot exit 0, capture all black - the X server resets when its last client disconnects; Xvfb -noreset fixes it) and the fact parser silently DROPPED host_x11_socket_present because its regex was [a-z_]+ and the key contains digits. The verdict script now requires each I4 fact to be OBSERVED rather than merely un-contradicted. DEVIATION: OBS was not run inside the container - ffmpeg x11grab was - because step 4 measured OBS carrying 317 MB of bundled surface including an embedded Chromium; journaled as goal-over-letter, and OBS-in-a-container is recorded as UNMEASURED rather than refused. The Dabbler extension is NOT installed in the image, so this proves the capture path is isolated and does NOT prove the Work Explorer renders under software rendering.

Named from the runs rather than from theory: the captured window is titled Welcome - capture - Visual Studio Code, on a bare X display with NO window manager, so no title-bar controls, no Windows chrome, Linux font rendering throughout. The trade is not slightly worse video - it is the right tool for one job and the wrong tool for the other. For proving a UI behaves, the container is good and the host path can see the host screen; for training staff who run Windows, the container puts the wrong product on screen in the first three seconds. The operator accepted the fidelity cost on 2026-08-16 AND bounded it the same day by ruling Sessions 7 and 8 record the host; this session endorses that split on evidence. Recommendation: keep the container as an internal VERIFICATION capability, do not promote it to a shipped feature here, and note the Session 4 host recorder stays gated closed on its own FAIL - two paths, two verdicts, neither a licence for the other.

Honoured. The Azure VDI research was completed on 2026-08-16 before this session started (docs/proposals/2026-08-16-azure-virtual-desktop-as-a-recording-target.md) and nothing in this session extended it, built on it, or created an Azure resource. Its two VERIFY-FIRST items stand, including that AVD screen-capture protection has a client-and-server mode which would block exactly this recorder by design.

Round 1 discovery (2-way fan-out, gpt-5-6-sol, spec-conformance and failure-scenario lenses) returned ISSUES_FOUND with 8 records = 4 distinct Majors, both lenses agreeing on all four. Round 2 supplementary found a fifth Major. THREE OF THE FIVE WERE FALSE PASSES IN MY OWN VERDICT SCRIPT. All five remediated, nothing waived, no threshold moved - the criteria file is byte-identical to the pre-run commit and the verdict refuses to score a measurement whose stamped digest does not match. F1 ffmpeg/stock-VS-Code substitution: OBS installed and RUN in the container (it works - and does NOT meet the predeclared I2 instrument, 0.085 vs 0.90, reported as such rather than by moving the bar), published 0.51.0 VSIX installed and asserted. F2 I5 certified the set cardinal degradation guarantee without testing it: built a real capture entrypoint that always writes a manifest and never throws; all three variants drive it; postconditions scored per variant. F3 I6 had no induced failure: cleanup moved into a finally, a real mid-run exception thrown, zero-byte and temp files counted inside and outside. F4 cost record incomplete and self-contradictory: --no-cache cold build (57.2s, because podman rmi alone keeps the layer cache and reported 2.9s - the same defect one layer down), all four required fields now present and SCORED on presence. F5 (supplementary, most serious) the plugin probe launched the operator LIVE OBS config which carries a webcam and microphone: now seeds its own empty collection, asserts zero live source kinds in OBS own log, and stashes/restores the operator sentinel markers instead of deleting them. Round-1 acceptance harness had one EXECUTABLE criterion still failing after the first fix - it required exact set equality with the declared variant names - so the podman-machine-stopped substitution was withdrawn and the machine is now stopped for real with a VERIFIED restart (stopped=true restored=true); journaled as a reversal of my own earlier decision. Verdict after remediation: PASS 7/7, 3/3 clean runs.
**Required portion of the full test suite.**
**Close-out.**

CORRECTED RE-LOG of the entry first written as step 2, which was wrong: step 2 is a planned spec step (set the pass criteria) and logging unplanned work under its number displaced it from the projection. Unplanned work gets a number past the plan, not a planned one. Content unchanged: recorded the operator direction that arrived before this session started, as spec and journal rather than as chat. Two amendments - the pointer feedback, and two tutorial-video sessions taking the set from six sessions to eight (7 records the single-module tutorial after making the pointer visible; 8 records the multi-module tutorial and is now set-terminal, so Session 6 closes mid-set). Diagnosed the cursor report before writing it down: capture-side cursor drawing was already ON in both backends, and the gap is that synthesised debug-protocol clicks never move a pointer, which makes it driver work in two different shapes. uatComponents grew to seven; the S1 test pinning those names by name rather than by count was updated with it, and the Training Publication reservation was marked TRIGGER FIRED because a public audience now exists. Four decisions journaled: three under operator authority (the extension, the pointer placement and ordering, the toy-project ruling as external-consequence), one under AI authority (the inventory growth).

Ran spec_admission against the amended spec, which is the check the authoring guide says to run at authoring rather than discover at hour three. It reported FOUR sessions over the 7-step cap - and two of them (5 and 6) were already over before this amendment, added by Session 4 this morning with no exception declared, so the amendment did not create that condition but would have quietly doubled it. Trimmed where trimming was honest rather than excepting by default: Session 7 merged capture and time-compression into one pipeline step (N=5 -> 4), and Session 8 folded its quality bar into the recording step and its publication conventions into the safety pass (N=4 -> 2, now under cap with no exception). Declared sessionSizeException for 5, 6 and 7 with per-session reasons; Session 5s reason names six declared work steps honestly rather than the four I first wrote, because two of its steps are a reading instruction and a guardrail. 277 targeted tests green.

The operator installed Podman Desktop, Podman 6.0.2 and initialised a machine. The machine does not start: podman machine start ends in "ssh error: machine not in running state", reproduced on a FRESHLY created machine so it is not a corrupted VM. Traced below Podman: its WSL machine does not use WSL systemd support at all, it launches systemd itself in a private PID namespace via /root/bootstrap, and that systemd starts and exits within about 25 seconds with an empty log, so sshd never listens and the ssh connection podman uses has nothing to reach. The Docker Desktop named-pipe warning printed alongside is a red herring. Most likely cause, stated as hypothesis not finding: Fedora 44 systemd on WSL 2.1.5.0 with a January 2024 kernel; wsl --update is the obvious first thing to try and is the operator's call. Recorded in s5-podman-bootstrap-failure.md including a wrong hypothesis of mine that had to be rolled back - adding [boot] systemd=true to the distro wsl.conf, which made the distro unbootable and was recovered by podman machine rm plus init after taking an export. The plugin-surface measurement is unaffected and needs no container, which is why the spec ordered it first.

UNBLOCKED. The operator ran wsl --update: WSL went from 2.1.5.0 / kernel 5.15.146.1 to 2.7.11.0 / kernel 6.18.33.2, and podman machine start succeeded on the first attempt after a wsl --shutdown. Confirms the hypothesis that was written down BEFORE the fix was attempted. Verified past the success message rather than trusting it - podman run pulled alpine and executed a container, reporting kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2, 20 CPUs and 32 GB in the VM (the 2GiB in podman machine list is a display default, not the live allocation). Also answered the operator offer to switch their WSL distro to Fedora: not needed, and it would have cost real effort for nothing - podman machine is its OWN Fedora 44 image in a distro named podman-machine-default, and their Ubuntu distro is separate and untouched by podman. What was two years stale was the WSL platform, which every distro shares.
